summary: Round 2 fixes correctly resolve all three actionable round-1 findings. The patterns.md CSRF guidance now matches the WebFlux classes actually imported in SecurityConfig.java (CookieServerCsrfTokenRepository, XorServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler), the security baseline statement now reflects the explicit /api/** authenticated rule sitting before the catch-all, and deployment.md surfaces SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE as production-critical hardening flags. No new issues introduced; all four documents are accurate against backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/security/SecurityConfig.java, .env.example, application.properties, and tech-spec Decision 12. The two optional architecture.md suggestions from round 1 were not addressed and remain optional — not blocking.

suggestions.suggestion: (Carried over from round 1, optional.) The phrase 'replaces JWT for auth' on the spring-session-data-mongodb line reads as a delta against an earlier plan rather than an authoritative current-state description. Consider 'used for stateful login sessions' or simply dropping the parenthetical — the rationale is captured in tech-spec / decisions.md.
suggestions.benefit: Documentation reads as authoritative current-state reference rather than a historical delta.

suggestions.suggestion: (Carried over from round 1, optional.) The 'Currently implemented' suffix lists `security` alongside feature modules; a future agent looking for `security` as a feature package may be briefly confused. Consider clarifying that `security` is the SecurityConfig package, not a feature module.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces ambiguity about the role of the security package.
